verdict.line: You lose if you eat Boomerang Throw poke and let Rage cap for free; you win if you catch him with E (Disdain) while his Hop is down.

brief.thesis: This is a 52.4% lane over 1131 games with the solo-kill edge on your side, and the reason is structural: mini Gnar's only gap-closer/escape is E (Hop), a 475-range leap on a 22-to-12s cooldown, and once it's down he has no way to avoid your E (Disdain) charge. The danger window flips entirely once his Rage bar caps and he transforms, because Mega Gnar trades his Hyper poke for a hard stun on W (Wallop) and an AoE slam on E. Your whole lane is reading which Gnar is in front of you and whether his dash is up.

theirWindow.when: Rage bar near max / just transformed
theirWindow.what: Mega Gnar's W (Wallop) is a hard stun and his E is now an area slam instead of an escape. Don't walk up to melee-trade here — hold Q (Corrosive Charge) at range and wait for him to use a cooldown or revert.

yourWindow.when: He just used E (Hop) to engage or reposition
yourWindow.what: Mini Gnar has no other dash and Hop's cooldown is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s, so this is your all-in window. Charge E (Disdain) onto him, land Q for the slow, and let W (Purge) prioritize him since it targets champions you've recently struck.

start.why: The 51.3% win rate over 979 games reflects that you need the sustain and trade damage to answer his Boomerang poke while you close distance early.

boots.why: Both his forms deal 100% physical damage — Hyper-empowered autos in mini form, raw AD burst in Mega form — so the flat reduction outvalues Swiftness here (50.9% over 902 games).

core.why: Armor shred plus haste lets you chain Q-E-W faster and keeps pace with his Rage-fueled Move Speed bursts.
The bonus health and tenacity-adjacent survivability are what let you eat a Mega Gnar W (Wallop) stun and live to punish the follow-up.
Stacking resistances scale across both of his damage types over a long game, and this path is the highest-sampled at 55.1% over 187 games.

situational.when: the game is stretching long and you need a chase/kite tool to catch Hop resets (61.7% over 133 games)
you need sustain damage to win extended trades instead of burst (56.9% over 51 games)
their comp has heal-heavy or extra AD threats stacking onto you

runes.keystoneWhy: It rewards exactly the pattern this lane wants — stick two or three hits on him in the window his Hop is down and the amp burst closes the fight before he can reset.

summoners.why: Ignite is run in 73.9% of games at 52.6% win rate and converts your solo-kill advantage directly — it's the finisher for the all-ins you take the moment his Hop is on cooldown.

playing.title: Track Hop, not his HP
playing.detail: His threat level is entirely gated by whether E (Hop) is up. The second it's down, he can't escape your E (Disdain) charge — that's your green light to commit.

playing.title: Respect the Rage bar
playing.detail: Watch his combat meter. Right before it caps he transforms mid-fight into a form with a hard stun (W) and an AoE slam (E) — disengage rather than trade through the transformation.

playing.title: Displace him off his boomerang
playing.detail: Mini Gnar's Q refreshes its cooldown if he catches the returning boomerang. Use E (Disdain) to hurl him out of its return path and deny the reset.

playing.title: Sequence Q into W
playing.detail: W (Purge) prioritizes champions you've recently struck with other abilities, so always land Q (Corrosive Charge) first — it slows him into Purge range and guarantees the channel tracks him.

playing.title: Hunt the post-kit window
playing.detail: Right after Mega Gnar uses W (Wallop) or R (GNAR!), both his stun and his knockback are spent — this is your highest-value all-in, especially pre-level-9 while his Mega form is still short-lived.

playing.title: Don't facetank Mega Gnar's E
playing.detail: In Mega form, E is a ground-slam area attack, not a leap — standing next to him when he lands it is a free hit. Back off a step when he transforms before trading again.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, win rates, and pick rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the ability readings, cooldown numbers, and lane-timing calls are my own tactical analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep your distance to avoid being hit with Gnar’s (W). Try to engage and nuke Gnar once his (E) is on cooldown.
